meta.title: Supabase vs Firebase: Which one to choose in 2026? (data models, performance & use cases & code compared)
meta.description: Compare Supabase and Firebase architectural trade-offs, data modeling, query patterns, and indexing, and review side-by-side TypeScript to choose the right stack.

verdict: Choose Supabase if you want open-source flexibility, SQL, and full control over your data without vendor lock-in. Choose Firebase if you need a mature, fully managed NoSQL platform with deep Google Cloud integration and real-time sync. Evaluate based on your team's expertise and long-term needs.

comparison.toolA: Supabase is built on PostgreSQL, a powerful relational database with strong ACID compliance, complex queries, and extensions like PostGIS. It supports SQL and offers a RESTful API auto-generated from your schema. You can use row-level security for fine-grained access control.
comparison.toolB: Firebase uses Firestore, a NoSQL document database, and the Realtime Database for low-latency sync. Firestore scales horizontally and offers offline support, but lacks joins and complex transactions across collections. Data modeling requires denormalization and careful planning.

comparison.toolA: Supabase provides built-in authentication with email/password, OAuth providers, and magic links, backed by Postgres and row-level security. It offers a generous free tier and detailed user management via SQL. Features like multi-factor authentication are available but may vary by plan.
comparison.toolB: Firebase Authentication supports email/password, phone, OAuth, and anonymous sign-in, with easy integration into Google services. It includes multi-factor authentication and robust SDKs across platforms. However, customizing user data beyond the provided fields can be limited.

comparison.toolA: Supabase Realtime allows you to listen to database changes via WebSockets, with fine-grained authorization using row-level security. It also supports presence and broadcast for collaborative features. Performance depends on configuration and may require scaling for high-throughput use cases.
comparison.toolB: Firebase Realtime Database and Firestore both offer real-time synchronization, with offline support and automatic conflict resolution. Firestore's real-time listeners are robust and scale well for many apps. However, pricing can become complex with heavy read/write operations.

comparison.toolA: Supabase offers a free tier and usage-based pricing for its paid plans, with predictable costs based on database size, bandwidth, and compute. It can be self-hosted for full control, potentially reducing costs at scale. However, managing self-hosted instances requires operational expertise.
comparison.toolB: Firebase uses a pay-as-you-go model with free quotas, but costs can spike with high read/write volumes or bandwidth. Firestore's pricing is based on operations, which can be less predictable for read-heavy apps. Scalability is automatic, but cost optimization may require careful architecture.

comparison.toolA: Supabase is open-source and built on open standards like PostgreSQL, making it easy to migrate or self-host. You can export your data and schema without proprietary formats. This reduces long-term dependency on the platform.
comparison.toolB: Firebase is a proprietary Google platform, and while data can be exported, migrating away from Firestore or Authentication can require significant effort. The tight integration with Google Cloud services can increase lock-in. However, Firebase offers reliable managed infrastructure.

comparison.toolA: Supabase integrates with many third-party tools and services, and its open-source nature allows custom extensions. It provides client libraries for popular frameworks and supports edge functions for serverless logic. The ecosystem is growing but smaller than Firebase's.
comparison.toolB: Firebase has a mature ecosystem with deep integration into Google Cloud, including Cloud Functions, Hosting, and Analytics. It offers extensive SDKs and tools for mobile and web development. The ecosystem is vast but often tied to Google's services.

comparison.toolA: Supabase offers a clean dashboard, SQL editor, and auto-generated APIs, which can be efficient for developers familiar with SQL. The local development setup with Docker is straightforward. However, some advanced features may require more manual configuration.
comparison.toolB: Firebase provides a polished, intuitive console and CLI, with excellent documentation and quickstarts. Its emulator suite allows local testing. The experience is streamlined, especially for mobile developers, but complex queries in NoSQL can be challenging.

faq.q: Which tool is better for a project that requires complex queries and reporting?
faq.a: Supabase is generally better for complex queries because it uses PostgreSQL, which supports joins, aggregations, and advanced SQL. Firebase's NoSQL databases are not designed for ad-hoc complex queries and may require denormalization or external tools. If your app needs rich reporting, Supabase is likely the stronger choice.

faq.q: Is Firebase or Supabase more cost-effective for a startup?
faq.a: Both offer free tiers, but cost-effectiveness depends on your usage patterns. Supabase's pricing is often more predictable for database-heavy workloads, while Firebase's pay-as-you-go model can lead to unexpected costs with high read/write operations. Startups should estimate their expected usage and compare both pricing models carefully.

faq.q: Can I self-host Supabase or Firebase?
faq.a: Supabase is open-source and can be self-hosted, giving you full control over your data and infrastructure. Firebase is a proprietary Google service and cannot be self-hosted. If self-hosting or data sovereignty is a requirement, Supabase is the only option.

faq.q: Which platform has better real-time features?
faq.a: Firebase is often praised for its mature real-time synchronization, especially with Firestore and the Realtime Database, which handle offline scenarios well. Supabase Realtime is capable and integrates with Postgres, but may require more configuration for high-scale use. For simple real-time sync, Firebase may be easier; for custom real-time with SQL, Supabase is flexible.

Both provide robust authentication, but they differ in customization. Supabase Auth is built on Postgres and allows you to extend user data with SQL, while Firebase Auth is easy to integrate but offers less flexibility for custom user fields. Consider whether you need deep integration with your database or just standard auth flows.

faq.q: Is vendor lock-in a concern with either platform?
faq.a: Supabase reduces lock-in because it's open-source and based on PostgreSQL, making it easier to migrate. Firebase is proprietary, and while data export is possible, migrating away from its specific APIs can be time-consuming. If long-term portability is a priority, Supabase is the safer choice.

faq.q: Which tool is more scalable for a large-scale application?
faq.a: Both scale, but in different ways. Firebase is designed for automatic horizontal scaling and is used by many large apps. Supabase scales vertically and horizontally with Postgres, but may require more manual tuning for very high throughput. The best choice depends on your workload and team's expertise.

faq.q: How do the ecosystems compare for mobile development?
faq.a: Firebase has a strong mobile focus with SDKs for iOS, Android, and cross-platform frameworks, plus integrated services like Crashlytics and Analytics. Supabase also offers mobile SDKs but its ecosystem is smaller. For mobile-first apps that rely on Google services, Firebase may be more convenient.
